clue.text: Work at the deed in force

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other piece here

parts.note: to prise is to force something open
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: Someone toils at a legal document while it remains in force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deed in force' reads like legal wording, but 'force' is the verb prise, as in levering open a lid; 'the' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a skill is to work at it repeatedly, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Shrub is in teapot that's cracked

indicators.note: cracked means broken apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A plant has been placed in a broken teapot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' rearranges IS IN TEAPOT; 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a Mexican shrub with red bracts, popular at Christmas.

clue.text: Sailor has explanation for forgiveness

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
a solution explains a problem

explanation.surface: A seaman offers a reason in seeking pardon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolution is formal release from guilt, especially by a priest, so it is forgiveness.

clue.text: School staff

definitions.meaning: to school someone is to teach or coach them
a retinue of attendants following an important person

explanation.surface: Teachers and other employees at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is not employees but a body of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: To train is to school; a train is also a retinue of attendants.

clue.text: Extra cook — No. 2

parts.note: number two is second
to cook the books is to fiddle them

explanation.surface: An extra chef takes the deputy role.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse order in the clue; 'cook' means falsify, not prepare food.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing second fiddle means taking a subordinate supporting role, like an extra.

clue.text: Cartoonist exposes female in shock

indicators.note: in signals that the abbreviation goes within the word for shock

parts.note: to scare is to shock

explanation.surface: A satirical artist reveals a woman in a state of shock.
explanation.walkthrough: Gerald Scarfe is a British political cartoonist; 'exposes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Scarfe is a well-known British satirical cartoonist, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: I can't lose accommodation at the seaside

indicators.note: accommodation implies adjusting or rearranging to fit, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone sure of winning a room at a beach resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' rearranges I CAN'T LOSE; 'at the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The coastline is the shore where land meets sea, the seaside in a broad sense.

clue.text: Stood up for a flower girl

definitions.meaning: got to one's feet, past tense of arise
a girl named after a flower

explanation.surface: Getting up from a seat for a young woman selling blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'flower girl' suggests a wedding or a seller, but means a girl's name that is also a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past tense of rise, and also a flower that serves as a girl's name.

clue.text: God of Love is wound up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a sore is a wound

explanation.surface: Cupid's counterpart is tightly coiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' reads as tense, but WOUND is a noun giving SORE, turned by 'up'; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, counterpart of the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: Fashionable attitude, for example

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a stance is an attitude or position

explanation.surface: A trendy outlook is offered as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; the phrase 'for example' echoes 'for instance', which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or illustration, a direct synonym of example.

clue.text: Othello's lieutenant catches cold at exotic oasis

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters of oasis are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's soldier comes down with a chill at a strange desert spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches cold' looks like illness, but 'cold' is only its usual abbreviation, put in front of the reordered spring; 'catches' and 'at' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's tragedy Othello, Michael Cassio is the general's lieutenant.

clue.text: Violently mix liver and eggs, say

indicators.note: mix tells us to stir together the letters of the words

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to beat offal and eggs vigorously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix' rearranges LIVER, EGGS and SAY; 'and' only joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting aggressively means acting with hostile force, much as acting violently does.

clue.text: Carol calls for Mum at bedtime

definitions.meaning: read 'Mum' as silent: a demand for quiet when it is time to sleep

explanation.surface: A Christmas song, or a child crying for mother at lights-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not a mother here: 'mum' means silent, as in 'keep mum'.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol is the famous Christmas hymn; the second reading asks for a quiet evening.

clue.text: Not prepared to spray prince with dust

indicators.note: to spray scatters things about, so the letters are dispersed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Unready to shower a royal with powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spray' rearranges PRINCE and DUST; 'to' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An unscripted speech is delivered without a prepared text.

clue.text: It's not easy to cross an English poet embracing the French

indicators.note: embracing means the poet's name wraps around the French article

parts.note: Robert Bridges was an English poet laureate
les is the plural French word for the

explanation.surface: An English poet hugging the French is hard to get past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' is a link word. Robert Bridges was British Poet Laureate from 1913 to 1930.
explanation.definitionFit: A river without any spans over it is difficult to get across.

clue.text: Fish cooked as treat

indicators.note: cooked suggests something altered or prepared, so the letters of treat are mixed

explanation.surface: Fish prepared as a special dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges TREAT; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Meets bewildered males with Bess

indicators.note: bewildered means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Confused men get together with a woman named Bess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bewildered' rearranges MALES and BESS; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to gather or come together, as a group meets.

clue.text: Alien backing of monarch and the Queen

indicators.note: backing means the little word of is turned to run backwards

parts.note: a monarch's rule is a reign, the period on the throne
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: An outsider supports the King and his Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns OF into FO; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a person from another country, the same as one from abroad.

clue.text: Smooth aspects of Cromwell's horse

parts.note: to iron clothes is to smooth them
sides of an issue are its aspects

explanation.surface: Gentle features of the Lord Protector's steed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromwell's 'horse' means his cavalry, not one animal: they were nicknamed after him, Old Ironsides.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Cromwell's cavalry troopers in the English Civil War were known by this nickname.

clue.text: Hero from Spain led Channel Islands revolution

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, such as Jersey and Guernsey

explanation.surface: A Spanish champion headed an uprising in Jersey and Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges LED plus CI.
explanation.definitionFit: El Cid, Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar, is the legendary medieval Castilian warrior and national champion of Spain.

clue.text: Moneybags gets rough girl in trouble

parts.note: a mill is old slang for a rough fight or punch-up
Iona is a girl's name
ire is anger, a cause of trouble

explanation.surface: A rich man ends up with a tough young woman who is in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'in' are link words; 'rough' is a noun, a scrap or fight, which old slang calls a mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneybags is a jocular name for a very wealthy person.

clue.text: Birth of a National and a Liberal

parts.note: Nat is an abbreviation of National
L stands for Liberal in British politics

explanation.surface: The arrival of one nationalist and one Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'a' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is an adjective meaning relating to one's birthplace or birthday, so 'of birth'.

clue.text: Saint Mark is not for women

parts.note: a tag is a mark or label

explanation.surface: The Gospel writer is barred to female company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint Mark' suggests the evangelist, but is split: S and TAG. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party or stag night is a male-only event, closed to women.

clue.text: Have supper with Miss Blyton on her return

indicators.note: her return means her name is turned around to run backwards

parts.note: Enid Blyton was a popular English children's author

explanation.surface: Eating an evening meal with a famous author when she comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word. Enid Blyton wrote the Famous Five books.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to eat a main meal, such as supper.

clue.text: Toy with end of shotgun

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the first half of the word

parts.note: a rifle is a gun

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles with the butt of a sporting gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shotgun' must be split into SHOT and GUN: the end of SHOT gives T, and GUN gives RIFLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with something is to toy with it, treating it lightly.

clue.text: Seven into one

parts.note: a group of seven musicians combined into one ensemble

explanation.surface: A sum of division that goes nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like arithmetic, but it describes seven performers forming one group.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of seven players, a single ensemble made of seven members.

clue.text: Smooth when in neutral

indicators.note: in places the word for when inside the colour word

parts.note: grey is a neutral colour
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Gliding easily when the car is out of gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neutral' suggests a gearbox, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasy can mean smooth and slippery, as a surface coated in oil is.

clue.text: Now's the time to break up bikes on Greek islands

indicators.note: to break up means the second piece splits the first open

parts.note: bikes are cycles
AD, anno domini, marks the present era, our time now

explanation.surface: Time to break up the bicycles parked on the Greek islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclades are a group of Greek islands in the Aegean Sea, including Naxos and Mykonos.
